subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw preserve a session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode while enforcing `message_tool_only` only in runtime delivery/tool execution, even when a particular turn requires message-tool delivery?
rationale: The change trades a more literal per-turn prompt instruction for a stable cache prefix, and only maintainers can confirm the intended safety and delivery contract across channels, Codex, and embedded-agent runs.

options.title: Adopt stable prompt-facing delivery
options.body: Keep prompt and tool guidance stable for a session, while runtime enforcement still requires message-tool delivery and rejects duplicate final delivery on affected turns.

options.title: Keep per-turn prompt directives
options.body: Retain the current explicit prompt behavior and accept the OpenAI automatic-cache churn until a different cache-safe design is approved.

options.title: Narrow to a provider-specific path
options.body: Apply the stable prompt mode only to OpenAI models, accepting provider-specific prompt assembly and added maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Adopt stable prompt-facing delivery
recommendation.body: Keep prompt and tool guidance stable for a session, while runtime enforcement still requires message-tool delivery and rejects duplicate final delivery on affected turns.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work spans the agent, provider, and Codex boundaries affected by this delivery-versus-prompt-cache decision.
